title: Liouville Energy Locates the Rightmost Zeta Zero
description: The sliding-window energy Q(N) of the Liouville function λ satisfies Q(N) = N^(2Θ+o(1)), where Θ is the supremum of the real parts of the zeros of ζ, and a bound along one sequence of N already locates Θ. Unconditionally Q(N) > 2.81N infinitely often, and Q(N)/N is bounded exactly when the summatory function of λ is O(√x). Changing λ on x^β primes can break the exponent when β > 1/2 and never when β ≤ 1/2. The archive contains the paper, a Lean 4 project (24 theorems) and three Julia programs. The Riemann hypothesis is not proved.
